scenes.text: The Statue of Liberty wasn't always green. She used to be shiny copper, like a brand new penny.
She was unveiled in New York on October twenty-eighth, eighteen eighty-six, as a gift from France.
Her skin is made of copper sheets only about as thick as two pennies stacked together.
Sea air and rain slowly reacted with the copper, and green started showing up around nineteen oh three.
In nineteen oh six, Congress set aside money to paint her, but people protested and the plan was dropped.
That green layer actually protects the metal underneath from wearing away.
Which color do you think looks better, copper or green?

title: The Statue of Liberty used to be copper-colored 🗽
caption: Lady Liberty was unveiled on October 28, 1886, shiny copper like a new penny. Sea air turned her green over about 20 years, and that green patina now protects her skin! 🗽
